issue_request: FHIR-55422 was an Applied FHIR-core/FHIR-I R6 change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked that Attachment users not be forced to use the SHA-1-only Attachment.hash element when another integrity-check algorithm is already used; the approved resolution was a repeatable Attachment-scoped alternate hash extension with 1..1 algorithm Coding and 1..1 hash string components.
initial_application: No Jira-tagged source commit was found in the core FHIR checkout. The matching application is fhir-extensions commit cb1c3600d7e7d201f5992dfdde18d7851f334d0c, followed by 0c72de5d, 2b046fd3, and 7d43dc06, which added and refined StructureDefinition-alternate-hash.xml plus integrity-check algorithm terminology inputs.
additional_context: Core source still defines Attachment.hash as the SHA-1 base64 checksum element, and Attachment is active/normative in source/fhir.ini. That remains correct because the Jira disposition chose a separate extension rather than changing Attachment.hash semantics. Confluence openEHR-FHIR datatype mapping minutes record the Attachment hash gap, the FHIR-55422 action, and a later note that the alternate hashing extension had been defined. FHIR-51236 is a later Resolved - change required issue about raw-byte base64 encoding and examples, but it is outside this default Applied/Published source-edit scope.
